glance.proposed_detail: Paid to a relative's account, with no receipt, no stages and nothing held back.

glance.ours_detail: Then five stages, each paid only against dated evidence, to an account in the builder's own name.

sections.checked: A search for the builder's name and number across Facebook, Google and Instagram, and for a registered business in his name. Nothing was found.

get_before_paying.document: Builder's full name, TRN and physical address, in writing
A bank account in the builder's own name, confirmed in writing
An itemised materials list with the supplier for each
Written agreement to the payment terms in section G
Start date, working days and completion date

next_steps.step: Tell the builder, politely, that you are not paying on Monday 5 October and that you will send some questions today.
Send the message in section I as it stands.
When the TRN arrives, check that the name on it matches the builder.
Agree the payment terms and the schedule in sections G and H in writing, with the share for each stage filled in.
Pay stage 1 only once the materials are on site with a supplier invoice in your name, and get a receipt.

payment_terms.instead: Nothing before the materials are on site. The first payment is stage 1 of the schedule.
payment_terms.why: Your money should never be ahead of what you can see.

payment_terms.instead: An account in the contractor's own name, confirmed in writing, or the materials supplier directly.
payment_terms.why: A payment has to be traceable to the contractor and the job.

payment_terms.instead: Bank transfer only. Never cash, and never a transfer to a person collecting on their behalf.
payment_terms.why: A transfer is a record. Cash is not.

payment_terms.proposed: One lump sum to the builder
payment_terms.instead: Supplier invoices made out in your name. Pay the supplier directly if the contractor agrees.
payment_terms.why: Materials in your name are yours if the job stops.

payment_terms.instead: Paid in stages, each only against the evidence in the payment schedule.
payment_terms.why: Money follows progress you can see from abroad.

payment_terms.instead: Within two working days of the evidence arriving, so the contractor is never kept waiting once the work is proven.
payment_terms.why: Protects the contractor as much as you. Fair terms are easier to hold them to.

payment_terms.instead: A written receipt for every payment, dated, naming the stage.
payment_terms.why: Your record of what has been paid and for what.

payment_terms.instead: Paid only once a snag list is agreed and every item on it is signed off.
payment_terms.why: Finished needs a definition both of you signed.

payment_terms.instead: Each stage fixed in Jamaican dollars in writing, so an exchange rate move does not change what is owed.
payment_terms.why: Removes an argument before it starts.

payment_terms.instead: If no work happens for ten working days without a written reason, no further stage is paid until you have both agreed a new date in writing.
payment_terms.why: Gives you a clear point at which to act.

payment_terms.instead: No extra work is paid unless it is agreed in writing before it starts.
payment_terms.why: The most common way a job goes over.

sections.ask_the_builder:
Hi Test Builder, thank you for the quote. Before we go ahead, could you send me the following in writing, please:

1. Your full name or business name, your TRN and a physical address.
2. The bank account you would like to be paid into, in your own name.
3. An itemised list of the materials, with the supplier for each, and the invoices made out in my name.
4. A start date, how many working days the job will take, and a completion date.
5. What happens if the job runs late, and what happens if I need to stop the work.
6. Whether you hold any insurance, and whether anyone else will be working with you.
7. Whether you give any guarantee on the work once it is finished.

On payment, I would rather not pay up front. I would like to pay in stages as the work goes, each stage paid promptly once I have the photos or receipts for it, by bank transfer to your own account. I will send you the stages so we can agree the amount for each one together before anything starts.

If anything changes once you are on site, please stop at that point and write down what changed, and what it does to the time and the price, so we can agree it before carrying on.

Thank you, I look forward to hearing from you.

checklist.why: You need to know who you are agreeing with.
The only formal way to identify them later.

checklist.item: Verifiable address and a number other than WhatsApp
checklist.why: A WhatsApp number can disappear overnight.
Past work others can see is the best evidence of a track record.
Fixes what was offered and when.

checklist.item: Quote itemised by element of work
checklist.why: Lets each stage be matched to what it pays for.
Shows how much of the money is materials you could own.
Stops cheaper materials being swapped in.
Decides who you pay for them.

checklist.item: Who owns the materials once paid for
checklist.why: Decides whether they are yours if the job stops.
Somebody has to count what arrives.
Often left out, then charged as extra.
The single biggest source of risk on a job like this.
checklist.note: 70 percent to start, balance on completion.

checklist.item: Payment to an account in the contractor's own name
checklist.why: Makes every payment traceable to the contractor and the job.
checklist.note: A relative's account was asked for.

checklist.why: Cash leaves no record.

checklist.item: What the client is exposed to at each stage
checklist.why: Tells you the most you could lose at any moment.
Your record of what has moved.
Covers damage or injury on your property.

checklist.item: Who else will work on site
checklist.why: You should know who is in your house.
Says what happens if something fails after they leave.
Some work needs the local authority told before it starts.

checklist.item: Start date, working duration and completion date
checklist.why: Without dates, nothing is ever late.

checklist.item: What happens if the contractor is late
checklist.why: Gives you a point at which to act.

checklist.item: What happens if the client stops the work
checklist.why: Protects the contractor as well as you.
Agreed now, it is a process. Agreed later, it is a fight.

lines: Take out old bathroom suite and tiles. Supply and fit new toilet, basin, shower and tiles.
Fix back wall, block and render.
Labour J$222,222 (TEST FIGURE). Total J$333,333 (TEST FIGURE)

findings.heading: Most of the money is asked for before work starts
findings.body: The quote asks for 70 percent to start and the balance when the job is finished. There is no stage in between, and nothing is held back at the end.
findings.why: Once most of the money has moved, you have very little left to hold if the work stops, slows or is not what was agreed. From abroad, you would be relying entirely on goodwill.
findings.action: Replace it with the payment terms in section G and the staged schedule in section H, where money follows evidence.

findings.heading: Payment asked for into a third party's account
findings.body: The builder asked for the deposit to be sent to his cousin's account so that the materials could be bought on Monday.
findings.why: A payment to someone who is not the builder is very hard to trace back to the job if something goes wrong.
findings.action: Pay only into an account in the builder's own name, or pay the materials supplier directly.

findings.heading: No business is named on the quote
findings.body: The quote carries a first name, a trading description and a WhatsApp number. There is no business name, no TRN and no address, and the reviewer's search found no business registered under this name.
findings.why: If something goes wrong there is nobody formally identifiable to hold to the agreement, and no way to check a track record.
findings.action: Ask for his full name, TRN and a physical address, and check them before paying anything.

findings.heading: Materials are not itemised and ownership is not stated
findings.body: The quote gives one line for materials with no list, no specification and no supplier.
findings.why: You cannot tell what you are paying for, or whether the materials are yours if the job stops.
findings.action: Ask for an itemised list and for the supplier invoices to be made out in your name.

findings.heading: No start or finish date
findings.body: The quote says the work will start soon. No dates or duration are written anywhere.
findings.why: Without dates there is no point at which the job is late, so there is nothing to act on if it drags.
findings.action: Agree a start date, a number of working days and a completion date in writing.
